html:
Egyptian Harar was the territory around the walled Muslim city of Harar, in what is now eastern Ethiopia, held by Khedivate Egypt from 1875 to 1885, together with the Somali ports of Zeila and Berbera. The map shows it in 1880, and still in 1900, though by then the land belonged to Ethiopia.

Khedive Ismail wanted an African empire along the Nile and the Red Sea. In 1875 an Egyptian force took Harar and ended the rule of its emirs. Egypt's wider war with Ethiopia that year and the next ended in defeat.

When the Mahdist revolt in Sudan cut Egypt off, it pulled out of Harar in 1885 and left a local emir in charge. Two years later Menelik II of Shewa defeated him and added Harar to the Ethiopian Empire. Britain took over the coast as British Somaliland. The old city, Harar Jugol, is now a World Heritage site.
